description: A molecular diagnostics director must choose one of three clinically plausible cases for the laboratory's single overnight rapid whole-genome sequencing run and finalize the test scope, specimen handling, and authorization record, with input from genetics, laboratory operations, genetic counseling, and utilization management.

shared_context.S1: The laboratory has one overnight rapid whole-genome sequencing run available for only one of three cases: Alder, Birch, or Cedar.
shared_context.S2: All three cases have been referred for potentially actionable genetic information, and the referring teams are awaiting a final laboratory decision.
shared_context.S3: Laboratory policy gives the overnight run to a case that satisfies the clinical-actionability, specimen-adequacy, consent-scope, and payer-authorization requirements.
shared_context.S4: The final report must identify the selected case, the assay, the specimen amount and handling instruction, the consent scope, and the authorization status.
shared_context.S5: Before the run is released, Dr. Morris follows the laboratory's routine multidisciplinary huddle and checks with genetics, laboratory operations, genetic counseling, and utilization management.

PF1.text: Case Alder has a medication-selection decision that depends on a rapid whole-genome result, so the clinical team has designated Alder as the clinically actionable priority for this overnight run; Dr. Shah documented the decision in his service note, but the note has not yet reached the laboratory queue.

PF2.text: Case Alder's received specimen contains exactly 3.2 mL of viable blood, meeting the laboratory's 3.0 mL minimum, and it must be processed with the standard EDTA extraction protocol; Mei verified both details at accession.

PF3.text: The patient for Case Alder signed consent for both primary findings and secondary findings, so the report scope must be recorded as primary_and_secondary_findings; Carlos completed the consent review this afternoon.

PF4.text: The payer approved rapid whole-genome sequencing for Case Alder under authorization code UM-4821, with the authorization status recorded as approved; Nadia received the approval notice but has not yet entered it in the laboratory authorization screen.

acceptance_conditions: Case Alder must receive the overnight run because it is the clinically actionable priority.
The assay must be rapid whole-genome sequencing.
The specimen amount must be recorded as exactly 3.2 mL and the handling instruction must be standard EDTA extraction.
The consent scope must be recorded as primary_and_secondary_findings.
The authorization status must be approved under authorization code UM-4821.
The clinical-actionability fact must be spoken by its owner and cited by the decision-maker as justification.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'overnight_run_release' and c['target'] == 'Alder' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The clinical geneticist's designation changes the selected case to Alder and identifies rapid whole-genome sequencing and the Alder run-release commitment as the appropriate clinical plan.
The accessioned 3.2 mL volume and standard EDTA extraction instruction change the specimen fields from unspecified handling to exactly 3.2 mL with the required protocol.
The completed consent review changes the report scope to exactly primary_and_secondary_findings rather than an unspecified or primary-only scope.
The payer notice changes the authorization fields to approved and the exact authorization code UM-4821.
